questions.q: Why does a thrust stand take a zero both before and after a run?
options: To average the HX711 noise over two segments
To check that the weights did not shift on the hanger
To subtract the zero drift over time
To recompute the scale k from two points
questions.explain: The motor and ESC warm the bar: the zero shift of a cheap bar is up to ±0.2 % FS per 10 °C (±10 g for 5 kg). In the example the zero moved by +3.29 g over the run; the correction is linear in time between the "before" and "after" zeros.

questions.q: What happens if a Wi-Fi interrupt holds the HX711 PD_SCK high for longer than 60 µs in the middle of a read?
options: The HX711 enters power-down and the sample is corrupted
The HX711 switches to channel B with gain 32
The sample just arrives one clock later, with no error at all
The HX711 switches to 80 samples per second
questions.explain: Per the datasheet, PD_SCK high > 60 µs means power-down mode. That is why the 25 read pulses run in a critical section (portENTER_CRITICAL), and Wi-Fi is best turned off during the run. The channel and gain are selected by the number of pulses (25/26/27), and the rate by the RATE pin.

questions.q: A fragment of stand processing (MN4006 KV380, 15×5, 24 V). Where is the efficiency lost?
options: In the prop: C_T is well below the datasheet
In the drive: C_T as in the datasheet, but g/W lower
Nowhere: −9 % fits within the uncertainty
In the thrust channel: the load cell reads low at high thrust
questions.explain: C_T matches the datasheet, so the prop and the thrust measurement are fine. g/W is consistently 8–9 % lower at the same thrust, while U(k=2) is only ±1.3 %: this is a systematic effect of the electrical part (ESC, wiring, where the voltage is measured).

questions.q: Calibration: zero 84 254 counts, k = 432 counts/g, no drift. The raw sample is 421 646. What is the thrust?
questions.explain: T = (raw − b)/k = (421 646 − 84 254)/432 ≈ 781 g. 976 g is what you get if you forget to subtract the zero.

questions.q: C_T and C_P are defined through n (rev/s) and D (m). How do you compute the figure of merit FM correctly?
options: FM = C_T / C_P
questions.explain: FM = P_id/P_shaft, P_id = T^1.5/√(2ρA), A = πD²/4. Substituting gives C_T^1.5/(√(π/2)·C_P). The form with √2 is for helicopter coefficients based on Ω·R; with propeller coefficients it understates FM by 11 % (0.64 instead of 0.72 in the example).

questions.q: A 5 kg bar, 1.0 mV/V, the bridge powered from the HX711 AVDD, channel A ×128. About how many counts per gram?
questions.explain: The HX711 full scale is ±0.5·AVDD/128 and the bridge output is S·AVDD, so the measurement is ratiometric: 0.001·128·2²³/0.5 ≈ 2 147 484 counts per 5000 g, about 430 counts/g. 2.1 million is for the bar's whole scale.

questions.q: Bidirectional DShot on an MN4006 (24 poles) shows 74 000 eRPM. The mechanical RPM?
questions.explain: RPM = eRPM / (poles/2) = 74 000/12 ≈ 6167. Dividing by 24 (3083) is a common mistake: you have to divide by the number of pole pairs (12), not by the number of poles.

questions.q: Why does the stand firmware check the current and the timeout every 100 ms on their own schedule rather than in the "HX711 ready" branch?
options: So the INA226 has time to average 16 samples
So the HX711 does not enter power-down during I²C
The timer is needed so the ESC gets exactly 50 Hz
If the HX711 drops out, the branch never runs and the throttle is not cut
questions.explain: If DOUT never goes low (the sensor dropped out), the code in the ready branch never runs. Safety must not depend on it: the 0.5 s timeout and the current limit are checked every 100 ms, and nothing else in the loop may block for long. The PWM frequency is set by the LEDC hardware.
